item.text: The CSV has three specimens per material, with ten points per specimen. The measurements remain close to linear through the recorded strain range, so I’m fitting the full measured range and will pool specimens by material while retaining specimen-level variation in the summary. I’ll report the regression intercepts and R² so the fit is transparent.

# Tensile test results

Elastic modulus was estimated as the slope of an ordinary least-squares linear regression of stress (MPa) on strain, pooling all three specimens for each material. The fit used the full measured range, strain 0.0002–0.0020 (0.02–0.20%). Moduli are reported in GPa; regression intercepts are in MPa.

| Material | Elastic modulus (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² | Specimen slopes (GPa) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Aluminum | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.99834 | AL-1: 70.12, AL-2: 67.38, AL-3: 70.64 |
| Steel | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.99844 | ST-1: 201.22, ST-2: 197.28, ST-3: 198.69 |
| Titanium | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.99788 | TI-1: 114.62, TI-2: 117.83, TI-3: 117.23 |

The pooled fits are strongly linear over the sampled interval. The specimen slopes show repeatability within each material, while the fitted intercepts capture small offsets in the measured stress values. Because the dataset provides no unloading or yield-point characterization, these values describe the apparent modulus over the recorded interval.

![Stress–strain data and pooled linear fits](stress_strain_fits.svg)

The fits have R² values above 0.997. The report includes specimen-level slopes, fit intercepts, and the fitting range.
